forwardMerge.whatMoved: Six files of the pull request's own diff moved between those two heads, found by hashing each file's contribution separately rather than taking anyone's word: three joined it (packages/envoy-client/src/replay.ts, packages/envoy/cmd/listener/api.go, packages/envoy/docs/architecture.md) and three changed (packages/envoy/.changes/unreleased/INFRA-745-denied-publish-is-named.yaml, packages/envoy/AGENTS.md, packages/envoy/internal/bus/confirm.go). The round-2 fix still holds: five comments in quick succession on an issue routed to a session, so one batch sends one owner topic five times and one agent subject five times through one window, leave all five events at attempt_count 3 evenly, /metrics carrying reason="denied" 40 with no reason="failed" series, and a grep of the whole process log for "NATS is unreachable" finding nothing. proof.criterion: review round 1's important finding: the change turns a denied JetStream publish into the listener's 403, which made main's listener documentation false. The behaviour is real, the documentation now states it, and the client meets a permanent refusal instead of a retried outage.
proof.surface: the real envoy-listener binary built at this merge head, connected to a real nats-server 2.15.1 whose authorization is Envoy's own production renderer with notifications.> removed from this listener's user, over HTTP at http://127.0.0.1:9030; then this workspace's own packages/envoy-client/src/transport.ts createEnvoyClient, the path a Legion session's publish takes, with an injected fetch counting HTTP attempts
proof.command: go build -o rigtest/envoy-listener ./cmd/listener; run it with PORT=9030 ENVOY_MACHINE_ID=example-dispatch NATS_URLS=nats://127.0.0.1:4434 NATS_NKEY_SEED_FILE=out-denied/dispatch.seed; curl -sS -i -X POST -d '{"topic":"notifications.dispatch.issue.X-1.comment.created","message":"..."}' http://127.0.0.1:9030/v1/messages/publish; then bun run publish-denied.ts http://127.0.0.1:9030
proof.observed: HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden with no Retry-After header at all, and a body of {"error":"envoy: the message bus denied the publish under this listener's own permissions: bus: NATS denied the publish to \"notifications.dispatch.issue.X-1.comment.created\": nats: permissions violation: Permissions Violation for Publish to \"...\""}. That body opens with the Legion daemon's own publishDeniedPrefix constant, byte for byte - checked by reading the constant out of packages/daemon/internal/notify/notify.go and matching the live body against it - which is what makes notify.HTTPPublisher finish such a notice instead of retrying it without a cap. The client throws after exactly 1 HTTP attempt, carrying the denial's own words. The documentation now says all of this on main's own text: packages/envoy/docs/architecture.md:93-106 names both transports, says a topic the stream captures and POST /v1/messages/send are answered that 403 too, and states the client-visible change in those words; packages/envoy/AGENTS.md:2589-2590 say it in the send and publish rows.
proof.negativeControl: a listener built from the same source with packages/envoy/internal/bus at main@origin (async.go, confirm.go, nats.go and recovery.go restored, denials.go removed), on the same nats-server, the same grant and the same request, at http://127.0.0.1:9032: HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable with Retry-After: 1 and "envoy: the message bus did not answer: context deadline exceeded", and the same client against it makes 2 HTTP attempts rather than 1. So the 403, its wording and the end of the retry are this change's doing.

notFindings: The implementer's forward-merge comment and this tester's fingerprint name different files because they compare different windows, not because either is wrong; the reviewer's prose commits fall between this tester's verified head and the implementer's merge.

The listener's 403 body and the Legion daemon's publishDeniedPrefix are the same string, checked live rather than by reading both files; main introduced that coupling and this change is what makes a JetStream denial reach it.
The core publish path still reads the connection's last error (confirmPublished), unchanged by this round and sound there because sendCore republishes each unconfirmed send alone on the connection.

EnvoyApiError exposes no numeric status field to a caller that reads .status; both the 403 and the 503 report undefined there. That is main's error shape, identical on both sides of the control, and no part of this change.
forArchitect: The round passes. The reviewer's only important finding is closed on both halves: the behaviour it described is real - I drove the listener's publish route to a 403 with no Retry-After and the client to exactly one HTTP attempt, against a control built with internal/bus at main@origin that answers the same request 503 with Retry-After and two attempts - and the documentation now states it on main's own text. The forward merge's fingerprint changed, so this was a full round rather than bare gates: every criterion was driven again at the merge head, and the package main rewrote under the branch, cmd/listener, was run here because its lane is not one main requires.
